newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond spreads flat, merger stirs junk.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond spreads flat, merger stirs junk.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were largely unchanged in a lackluster post-holiday session on Tuesday, while a thin new issue slate featured $400 million in 30- and 40-year debt from Coastal Corp.

High-yield issues were also thinly traded, but dealers said debt from Chancellor Broadcasting Co realized gains after the announced buyout by Evergreen Media Corp. Chancellor's recent issue of exchangeble preferreds reflected best demand, trading up about three points to 103-1/2 bid, one source said.
After the Chancellor acquisition, Evergreen said it would then acquire $1.075 billion in Viacom Inc radio properties.
Viacom debt firmed by "a few" basis points in the investment grades market, traders said. Trade there was quiet, however, and volume in the debt was insignificant, they added.

At the same time, Viacom Inc Chairman Sumner Redstone on Tuesday said the company aims to cut its total debt by 20 to 40 percent over the next two to three years. Redstone spoke at the Cruttenden Roth growth stock conference in Laguna Nigel, California.
In other high-grades trade, dealers stressed spreads were unchanged with few markets made as players returned from the long President's Day holiday weekend.
In another variation from Tuesday's norm, however, traders said Citicorp's debt tightened two basis points after Moody's Investors Service said it may upgrade the credit.
New issuance was topped by $400 million Baa3/BBB-minus rated notes from Coastal Corp, won in a competitive sale by Smith Barney Inc.

A $200 million tranche of 7.42 percent 40-year debt was priced at 83 basis points over the T-bond. Another $200 million 30put10s were priced as 6.70s to yield 42.9 basis points over the 10-year T-note.

Also on Tuesday, PPG Industries issued $200 million A1/single-A rated five- and 15-year debt through a Credit Suisse First Boston syndicate. The five- years were priced as 6.25s to yield 29 basis points over the Treasury curve and the 15-years were priced as 6.875s to yield 60 basis points over the curve. The latter tranche has a make-whole call.
Back in high-yields, traders reported buying activity surrounding TCI Satellite Entertainment's new $352 million senior subordinated and senior discount notes.
Argosy Gaming Co's mortgage notes were quoted 1/4 to 1/2 point higher at 83-1/2.

The company late Friday reported fourth quarter per share loss of $0.34 compared with a profit of $0.04 from the same period one year ago. Gaming traders and analysts said the weak numbers were near expectations.

In new high-yield issues, Unifi Communications Inc issued $175 million overfunded 144A senior notes due 2004 at par to yield 14 percent. The deal was sold with warrants for 17.5 percent in Unifi equity, according to a syndicate source.
Capstar Broadcasting Partners sold $150 million of 12.75 percent 12-year zero coupon bonds in a 144a offering from BT Securities Corp. The deal was increased from $100 million.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond slipped 1/4 point in lethargic trade to yield 6.55 percent.
